**(i)** The probability density function, $f$, of a random variable, $X$, is given by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} k(x+3), & -3 < x < 3, \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$

Calculate
incertitudes: Question 3 : les points imprimés sont (10, 3) pour 13 au total. Lecture retenue : 10 pour la partie (i) ((a), (b), (c)) et 3 pour la partie (ii). Le bloc (i) n'étant pas ventilé par le sujet, 10 est porté par i.a.
Question 3 (ii) : l'équation à démontrer, $m^2 + 6m - 9 = 0$, a deux racines $-3 \pm 3\sqrt{2}$ ; seule $m = -3 + 3\sqrt{2} \approx 1.243$ appartient à l'intervalle $(-3, 3)$ : le corrigé le précise.

questions.corrige_markdown:
For a probability density function, the total area under the curve is 1:

$$\int_{-3}^{3} k(x+3)\,dx = 1$$

$$k\left[\frac{(x+3)^2}{2}\right]_{-3}^{3} = k\left(\frac{36}{2} - 0\right) = 18k = 1$$

**$k = \dfrac{1}{18}$.** (Then $f(x) = \dfrac{x+3}{18} \ge 0$ on $(-3, 3)$, so $f$ is a valid density.)

questions.enonce_markdown: **(ii)** If the median of $X$ is $m$, show that $m$ satisfies the equation $m^2 + 6m - 9 = 0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median $m$ is the value such that $P(X < m) = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Since the density is non-zero only on $(-3, 3)$, for $-3 < m < 3$:

$$P(X < m) = \int_{-3}^{m} \frac{x+3}{18}\,dx = \frac{1}{18}\left[\frac{(x+3)^2}{2}\right]_{-3}^{m} = \frac{(m+3)^2}{36}$$

Setting this equal to $\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$$\frac{(m+3)^2}{36} = \frac{1}{2} \;\Rightarrow\; (m+3)^2 = 18 \;\Rightarrow\; m^2 + 6m + 9 = 18$$

$$\boxed{m^2 + 6m - 9 = 0}$$

which is the required equation. **Remark.** Its roots are $m = -3 \pm 3\sqrt{2}$; only $m = -3 + 3\sqrt{2} \approx 1.243$ lies in $(-3, 3)$, so this is the median.
